units.title: Basic Word Order and 是
units.meaning: Subject + verb/adjective/object. Use 是 only for identity, category, or role.
units.structure: S + 是 + N / S + V + O
units.coreExplanation: Use this to stop translating English word-for-word. Chinese usually starts with the topic/person, then the action or description. 是 is not used before adjectives like busy, tired, good, or expensive.
units.whyItMatters: You will see this in beginner dialogue, sentence builder, listening questions, and TOCFL-style reading. Train it until you can produce it without translating word by word.
commonMistakes: Do not copy English word order when time/place appears.
Do not use 是 before adjectives such as 忙, 累, 好.
Keep the subject or topic clear before adding details.

units.title: 有, Numbers, and Measure Words
units.meaning: Use 有 for possession/existence and place numbers before measure words.
units.coreExplanation: Measure words are not decoration. They are part of the noun phrase. This unit trains 有, 一個, 兩個, 幾個 and basic counting in real sentences.
units.whyItMatters: You will see this in beginner dialogue, sentence builder, listening questions, and TOCFL-style reading. Train it until you can produce it without translating word by word.
commonMistakes: Do not put the measure word after the noun.
Use 兩 before measure words more often than 二.
有 is possession/existence, not a general linking verb.

可以 is permission/possibility, not the same as 會.

units.title: Reasons and Soft Contrast
units.meaning: Use 因為...所以 to explain reasons and use 可是 to add soft contrast.
units.structure: 因為 reason, 所以 result / A, 可是 B
units.coreExplanation: This unit teaches why something happens and how to disagree or contrast politely.
units.whyItMatters: You will see this in beginner dialogue, sentence builder, listening questions, and TOCFL-style reading. Train it until you can produce it without translating word by word.
commonMistakes: Keep the reason and result logically connected.
因為可是 is not the pattern; use 可是 before the contrast clause.
Do not forget the result after 所以.

units.title: Compare and Prefer
units.meaning: Use 比 for comparison and 比較 for softer preference or degree.
units.structure: A 比 B Adj / S 比較 V/N
units.coreExplanation: Comparison is crucial for shopping, opinions, and choosing study actions.
units.whyItMatters: You will see this in beginner dialogue, sentence builder, listening questions, and TOCFL-style reading. Train it until you can produce it without translating word by word.
commonMistakes: 比 compares two clear things.
比較 can soften a preference without naming the second choice.
Do not place 比 after 比較.

units.title: If and Result
units.meaning: Use 如果 to set a condition and 就 to mark the result.
units.coreExplanation: This pattern turns beginner sentences into planning, advice, and test-style logic.
units.whyItMatters: You will see this in beginner dialogue, sentence builder, listening questions, and TOCFL-style reading. Train it until you can produce it without translating word by word.
commonMistakes: 如果 introduces the condition; 就 marks the result.
The condition usually comes before the result.
Do not use a result marker without a result clause.

units.title: Although and But
units.meaning: Use 雖然...可是 to show concession: even though A, B is still true.
units.structure: 雖然 A, 可是 B
units.coreExplanation: This is a key bridge to longer reading passages because it marks contrast across clauses.
units.whyItMatters: You will see this in beginner dialogue, sentence builder, listening questions, and TOCFL-style reading. Train it until you can produce it without translating word by word.
commonMistakes: 雖然 needs a real contrast after 可是/但是.
Do not repeat the same idea on both sides.
Keep the contrast clear and useful.

units.title: Intro to 把 Structure
units.meaning: Use 把 when the sentence focuses on what someone does to a specific object.
units.coreExplanation: Do not overuse 把. Use it when the sentence focuses on what someone does to a specific object.
units.whyItMatters: You will see this in beginner dialogue, sentence builder, listening questions, and TOCFL-style reading. Train it until you can produce it without translating word by word.
commonMistakes: Only use 把 with a specific known object.
The verb usually needs a result, direction, or location after it.
Do not use 把 for simple existence or liking.
